answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The atlas multiplier is published, charged in jetty, and knoll lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 640 identities would post 4957 proofs and burn roughly 56 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
